title: Veerendra Kumar Jain v. State of U.P. & Others
coram: Govind Mathur, C.J. & Saurabh Shyam Shamshery, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of; consumer relegated to the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman remedy
headnote: A grievance about two bills raised simultaneously for one electricity connection is a billing grievance to be raised before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (the forum reference being printed on the bill itself). The Court relegated the consumer to that remedy, to be considered on merits within 45 days, and continued the existing interim order until disposal.

holding_units.topic: Billing grievance (duplicate bills) belongs to the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman route
holding_units.question: Should the writ court adjudicate a complaint of two simultaneous bills, or is it for the Clause 7.10 forum?
holding_units.holding: It is for the Clause 7.10 forum. The consumer is relegated to the CGRF/Ombudsman under Clause 7.10 (the forum being noted on the bill), his application to be decided on merits within 45 days; the interim order continues until then.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Two bills raised simultaneously for one connection (No. 068335).

principle_tags.application: A duplicate-billing grievance is for the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman route in the first instance, not the writ court.
